product_name: Iowa Environmental Mesonet CONUS NEXRAD N0Q base reflectivity (NOAA WSR-88D) inside its domain + ECCC North American Radar Composite 1km rain (RADAR_1KM_RRAI, mm/h) / snow (RADAR_1KM_RSNO, cm/h) outside it
variable: N0Q base reflectivity dBZ (IEM domain); ECCC precipitation-rate rain/snow mapped to a compatible qualitative intensity (documented, not numerically equal)
spatial_resolution_source: IEM ~1km CONUS mosaic 5-min; ECCC 1km NA composite 6-min; canvas 3300x1600 (0.05 deg/px)
spatial_resolution_rendered: 1800x1175 canvas over lon [-93.0,-73.5], lat [40.5,49.5] (mean-value binning, no upsampling of source precision)
missing_data_treatment: IEM wins inside lon -130..-65/lat 22..50; ECCC outside it where RADAR_COVERAGE_*.INV is transparent (verified authoritative coverage: echoes fall outside INV-opaque); transparent elsewhere; never zero-filled; ECCC colors are rank-mapped, not dBZ.
shoreline_mask: assets/great_lakes_watermask.png — shared NOAA medium-resolution shoreline water mask (nautical-chart compilation, mean-high-water datum; snapped + polygonized once, full vertex precision, antialiased). Overlay alpha is multiplied by this mask and edge RGB is bled into transparent pixels (anti-fringe for bilinear clients), so every product shares one shoreline.

legend_scale_html: Precipitation intensity (NEXRAD N0Q base reflectivity, dBZ, OBSERVED radar echo): LOWEST 5 Very Light cyan/blue (drizzle, mist) → Light greens (~20-30: light rain/snow) → Moderate dark green (~30-40: steady rain/snow) → Heavy yellow/orange (~40-50: heavy rain) → Severe red (~50-60: severe storms, hail possible) → Intense magenta/purple (~60-70: violent storms, large hail) → HIGHEST+ 70+ Extreme white (destructive hail, debris). Same dBZ always shows the same color in every season — rain, snow, lake-effect snow, thunderstorms. No echo (no precipitation) stays see-through so the map underneath shows.

na_bounds.note: Authoritative common geography for the four North American live layers (precipitation_na, air_temperature_na, cloud_cover_na, wind_na). Every NA builder bins its own source grid onto this exact canvas, so the four overlays align in Google Earth. Degrees per pixel: 0.05 x 0.05 (square). This boundary is a bounding extent enclosing the buffered landmass; it does not imply valid source data everywhere — areas without valid source data stay transparent.

LIVE PRECIPITATION — NORTH AMERICA

Precipitation intensity (NEXRAD N0Q base reflectivity, dBZ, OBSERVED radar echo): LOWEST 5 Very Light cyan/blue (drizzle, mist) → Light greens (~20-30: light rain/snow) → Moderate dark green (~30-40: steady rain/snow) → Heavy yellow/orange (~40-50: heavy rain) → Severe red (~50-60: severe storms, hail possible) → Intense magenta/purple (~60-70: violent storms, large hail) → HIGHEST+ 70+ Extreme white (destructive hail, debris). Same dBZ always shows the same color in every season — rain, snow, lake-effect snow, thunderstorms. No echo (no precipitation) stays see-through so the map underneath shows.

Sources: Iowa Environmental Mesonet CONUS NEXRAD N0Q base reflectivity (NOAA WSR-88D) inside its domain + ECCC North American Radar Composite 1km rain (RADAR_1KM_RRAI, mm/h) / snow (RADAR_1KM_RSNO, cm/h) outside it
Precedence: 1) IEM opaque echo pixels inside the IEM effective domain. 2) ECCC rain/snow intensity outside the IEM domain where ECCC dynamic coverage = 1. 3) Transparent elsewhere. Coverage masks (ECCC RADAR_COVERAGE_*), never alpha-zero, decide the domain. Overlapping pixels: IEM wins; ECCC never painted on top of IEM.
